# Current state — lege-docwrite

What the project believes right now: live terms, constraints, policies and requirements, and what has been found or assessed. Decisions have their own view, `DECISION-HISTORY.md`.

## Policies

## Requirements

### PageUp/PageDown move exactly one physical page or spread

`proposed` · `@docwrite.req.exact-page-navigation/1` · scope `all` · topic `navigation`

PageDown always lands on the top of the next physical page and PageUp on the previous;
in spread mode they move one spread. Continuous mouse or trackpad scrolling stays
continuous during the gesture and settles magnetically onto the nearest page (or spread)
when the gesture ends. Jumps by page number, chapter, outline entry and search result are
deterministic.

### Minimal appearance and direct navigation for long-form writing

`proposed` · `@docwrite.req.minimal-writer-navigation/1` · scope `all`

The writer should look barebones and terminalesque and prioritize low latency
for books and large articles. Page Up, Page Down and seek by page number are
sufficient navigation for the current work. Do not introduce novel or
unnecessary viewing modes or navigation chrome. Navigation should reuse
the laid-out manuscript and remain predictable on long documents.

### Typing never waits on work unrelated to the edited paragraph

`proposed` · `@docwrite.req.typing-latency/1` · scope `all` · topic `typing-latency`

The hot path is key event → edit transaction → text mutation → reshape the affected
paragraph → incremental repagination to convergence → damage → present. Nothing else
runs on it: spell checking, image decoding, citation processing, index rebuilding,
search indexing, autosave serialization and export are asynchronous. For ordinary
typing in a 500-page book the application spends only a few milliseconds before handing
the frame to the presenter, and keypress-to-present latency is a regression gate.

## Observations

### cosmic-text LayoutRun.text is the whole buffer line, not the run fragment

`verified` · `@docwrite.observation.cosmic-text-run-text-is-full-line/2` · scope `path "crates/liminal-reader/src/document/markdown/layout.rs"`

cosmic-text 0.19 LayoutRun.text is the whole buffer line, not the run's
visible fragment: every wrapped run of a line reports the identical full
text, and only the run's glyph byte range (cluster indices, restarted per
buffer line) delimits what it shows. Slicing run.text per run repeats the
full paragraph on every wrapped line; at raster the over-long text shapes
unwrapped and spills past the content edge. The reader's shaper now cuts
each run's text from its glyph range against per-line base offsets, with
regression tests for reassembly, span bounds, cell-once tables and the
content edge. Observed while fixing duplicated paragraph lines, broken
tables and margin spill in the reader's Markdown engine (working tree
atop 21bc9e2, code uncommitted).

**supersedes** `@docwrite.observation.cosmic-text-run-text-is-full-line/1`

### M1–M5 were closed on synthetic test paths, not the editor

`verified` · `@docwrite.observation.milestones-closed-on-synthetic-paths/2`

At 8cc8d8f the ledger marked M1–M5 completed, but their evidence exercised
synthetic paths rather than the editor a writer uses. The window's Editor
cloned the Book and ran from_book on every paint and paged over a hardcoded
eight pages; the latency gate typed through Document::edit_page on a
one-line-per-page synthetic book. export_pdf put eight blocks per page, each
paragraph as one run in the invisible OCR text layer, so the PDF was
searchable but rendered blank. The one-line-per-page fast path put every
short paragraph on its own page whenever no chapter started recto. Chapter
titles never reached their openers or the Markdown/IDML exports, hyphenated
breaks drew no hyphen, and the binary could not open, save or export a book.

**supersedes** `@docwrite.observation.milestones-closed-on-synthetic-paths/1`

### Nothing in Lege-ecosystem shapes, breaks or hyphenates book text

`verified` · `@docwrite.observation.no-shaping-in-workspace/4`

No ecosystem crate depends on harfbuzz/rustybuzz/harfrust/swash directly; shaping is only
reachable through cosmic-text in lege-viewer's chrome. pdf-font (skrifa 0.44) parses
TrueType, CFF, Type1 and CID programs and exposes outlines, gid_for_char and advances but
no GSUB/GPOS. There is no unicode-linebreak, unicode-segmentation, hyphenation or
Knuth-Plass code. ropey is declared in the root workspace but no Lege crate uses it.

**supersedes** `@docwrite.observation.no-shaping-in-workspace/3`

### lege-pdf-write lacks what typeset-book PDF output needs

`verified` · `@docwrite.observation.pdf-write-gaps/5`

lege-pdf-write now embeds several glyph-font banks per page (GlyphLine.font), each
a caller-subset TrueType program with custom ToUnicode and widths, and draws gray
filled rectangles (PdfPageArtifact.fills). Still missing for book output: CFF /
FontFile3 embedding, general paths and RGB colour, link annotations and named
destinations, and a real structure tree (set_structure writes a flat list).

**supersedes** `@docwrite.observation.pdf-write-gaps/4`

> **Stale** — `watches "Cargo.toml"` was matched by `254a4bbf`, which touched `Cargo.toml`. See [REVIEW-REQUIRED.md](REVIEW-REQUIRED.md#lege-pdf-write-lacks-what-typeset-book-pdf-output-needs).

### pixelkit-shell needs presenter injection, IME, scroll phases and fuller key input

`verified` · `@docwrite.observation.pixelkit-shell-gaps/2`

pixelkit-shell hardcodes SoftbufferPresenter in resumed (the Presenter trait already
exists and has a Gpu backend variant); never calls set_ime_allowed or
set_ime_cursor_area, so IME events do not arrive; drops scroll TouchPhase and
pinch/magnify; keeps only the first char of Character input, emits no key-up and maps
few function keys; FrameTimer records paint and present but not input-to-present, and
tick is recorded as zero. Rendering repaints the full frame with no damage rects. The
single-line TextFieldState has no word motion, shift-extend, clipboard or undo.

**supersedes** `@docwrite.observation.pixelkit-shell-gaps/1`

### pixelkit-text cannot typeset books

`verified` · `@docwrite.observation.pixelkit-text-limits/2`

pixelkit-text parses only TrueType glyf outlines (no CFF, variable fonts or
collections), applies a fixed feature set (GSUB ccmp/liga, GPOS kern/mark/mkmk) with no
way to request smcp/onum/etc., skips GSUB type 5/7 and GPOS types 1/3/5/7/8/9, ignores
the ScriptList, has no bidi or UAX #14 line breaking, and caches rasterized whole strings
rather than glyphs.

**supersedes** `@docwrite.observation.pixelkit-text-limits/1`

### Reader clipboard runs on arboard with Wayland support

`verified` · `@docwrite.observation.reader-clipboard-arboard/1`

The reader's clipboard backend moved from copypasta 0.10 (X11-only ClipboardContext on Linux) to arboard 3.6 with default-features off plus wayland-data-control: arboard tries Wayland when WAYLAND_DISPLAY is set and falls back to X11, both round-tripped live, and copypasta is fully out of the lockfile. The lazy reconnect, external wl-copy/xclip/xsel fallback (non-blocking: holders never exit, so success is 'accepted stdin' with a reaper thread), status-bar notice, and stub-script tests are unchanged; no from-scratch crate was needed.

### Reader clipboard needs external-tool fallback on Wayland

`verified` · `@docwrite.observation.reader-clipboard-needs-external-fallback/1`

copypasta 0.10's ClipboardContext is X11-only on Linux (wayland_clipboard needs an external wl_display winit does not expose), so on a Wayland-only session SystemClipboard::new() failed once at startup and every copy/paste silently no-oped with only a stderr line — which read as 'cannot copy from Markdown'. ui.rs now connects lazily with reconnect-on-failure, falls back to wl-copy/wl-paste then xclip/xsel, and surfaces a persistent failure in the status bar. The Markdown substrate-to-text leg itself was intact (pinned by markdown_selection_copies_through_the_search_index).

> **Stale** — `watches "crates/liminal-reader/src/ui.rs"` was matched by `254a4bbf`, which touched `crates/liminal-reader/src/ui.rs`. See [REVIEW-REQUIRED.md](REVIEW-REQUIRED.md#reader-clipboard-needs-external-tool-fallback-on-wayland).

### Reader open classifies by content before extension

`verified` · `@docwrite.observation.reader-open-sniffs-content-first/1`

Document opening routed purely by extension at three gates (liminaldoc router, reader cli::is_markdown_path, app::open_document_engine), so a PDF with a wrong/missing suffix failed and text misnamed .pdf died in the PDF engine. Opening now classifies by content first (cli::classify_document_path: %PDF- magic scan, then text sniff, then extension), the launcher sniffs PDF magic before its extension check, and unknown binary keeps the PDF engine's honest parse error instead of rendering mojibake.

> **Stale** — `watches "crates/liminal-reader/src/cli.rs"` was matched by `254a4bbf`, which touched `crates/liminal-reader/src/cli.rs`. See [REVIEW-REQUIRED.md](REVIEW-REQUIRED.md#reader-open-classifies-by-content-before-extension).

### lege-viewer pages by line continuity and snaps only on command

`verified` · `@docwrite.observation.viewer-paging-is-line-continuity/3`

lege-viewer's PageUp/PageDown is line-continuity paging: paging_target makes the last
fully visible line the new top line, with notional-line and 8%-overlap geometric
fallbacks (lege-viewer/src/scroll/paging.rs). Nearest-page snap is an explicit command
(nearest_page_boundary, bound to S) and never happens automatically. Reusable, not
PDF-coupled: scroll/anchor.rs, frame.rs, damage.rs, diagnostics.rs, trace.rs, scene.rs,
present/*. The conductor/tile pipeline and the Pdf-variant artifact enums in
document/engine.rs assume read-only content.

**supersedes** `@docwrite.observation.viewer-paging-is-line-continuity/2`

### 200-page paste works; fullscreen scaling and page counter need attention

`verified` · `@docwrite.observation.writer-200-page-exercise/1`

On 2026-10-14 at code head 3b94ed4, the release Liminaldoc writer accepted
seven actual X11 clipboard pastes (600 paragraphs, 274199 text bytes,
42600 words) and native chapter commands. The saved/reopened manuscript
has exactly 200 pages with chapter starts 1,31,61,91,121,151,181. Every
chapter matches its clipboard payload byte for byte. A separate single
274199-byte live paste also saved without truncation. Live undo/redo of
the final chapter paste changed the count 200 -> 181 -> 200; saved content
still matched. Reopening the real window and seeking to 181 worked.

Release Editor measurements at 1100x800: bundle open 1.6 ms, first paint
34 ms, page seek/paint 0.77–1.17 ms, typing/paint at pages 1/100/200
1.15–1.61 ms (one paragraph shaped, one or two pages repaginated), one
whole-book paste/paint 31 ms, undo 2.9 ms, redo 26.8 ms, bundle save
0.69 ms, autosave snapshot clone 25 us. These are in-process timings,
excluding compositor/display latency. No timed 15-minute autosave soak
was performed in this exercise.

Two UI problems are reproducible in the live 2560x1600, 2x scale window:
(1) Minimal fullscreen fits a physical page to the entire screen width.
A 6x9 page becomes 3840 pixels tall, so only about 40% fits vertically.
Page Down still advances to the next physical page, requiring within-page
scrolling to see intervening text. This undermines the requested simple
page-key reading workflow. (2) The normal toolbar drops its page counter
when the last action row has insufficient spare width; the counter was
visible at 2200px width but absent at 2560px. toolbar.rs paint_toolbar
conditionally omits the status instead of reserving room for it.

This desktop also intercepts F11: Openbox rc.xml binds F11 to
ToggleFullscreen. Two F11 presses changed OS fullscreen state but neither
entered the writer blue mode (pixel assertion failed). Ctrl+Shift+F
reached the writer and produced 3.8 million blue pixels. This is a desktop
binding conflict, not evidence of a broken writer F11 handler. Document
the existing alternate shortcut; do not change global desktop settings.

Fixture and screenshots are retained by AKR scratch keep under
.agent/scratch/writer-200-pages. The release example long_manuscript
prepares clipboard chunks and independently verifies content, chapter
boundaries and timings of the native bundle made through the window.
